studies.title: Hyperplane Arrangements of Trained ConvNets Are Biased
studies.authors: Matteo Gamba; S. Carlsson; Hossein Azizpour; Mårten Björkman
measures: Early training showed strong negative-projection bias in almost all layers; toward the end, layers 2, 6, and 7 showed strong bias toward positive projections. The paper reports 82% training accuracy for VGG19.
For the last 8 convolutional layers, cumulative density remained constant at 50%; similar behavior was reported for the first 8 layers but not shown.
Layers 2–8 were described as heavily biased and critical to performance; the remaining convolutional layers could be reset to initialization without considerable performance loss.

Projection distribution shifted toward negative values in every layer except the first; during training, layers beyond the first shifted from about 50% negative projections toward all-negative projections.
Projection statistics were largely unbiased while training loss was approximately constant; around epoch 20, layers 2–5 became more biased as training loss started decreasing.
The step schedule reduced variance across runs and better separated strongly biased layers; the smooth schedule corresponded to less bias and smaller performance drops under weight reinitialization.
